subject: FedRAMP & ISO: evidence ownership, 3P attestations, and retention questions
messages:
From: Sara Paulson <sara.paulson@northbridge.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify evidence scope for FedRAMP/ISO review

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. As we prepare our security intake, two concrete questions came up from our audit team that we hope you can clarify before we start the questionnaire: 

1) For FedRAMP scoping, does Redwood intend to provide system logs (S3 snapshots + CloudTrail) for the last 12 months, or will you provide a sampling window tied to the audit window? Our auditors want to know the retention policy and whether snapshots are available on demand.

2) For ISO 27001 evidence, we track control ownership for evidence artifacts (who is the control owner and where the artifact lives). Do you have a canonical evidence matrix we can map to our auditor's control IDs?

Finally, our compliance lead also asked whether Redwood accepts third-party attestations (e.g., your upstream container registry provider or managed DB) as part of the SIG/CAIQ footprint, or whether you require customer-submitted vendor SOC reports.

If convenient, can we get a short note on ownership and sample artifacts so we can scope the SIG/CAIQ? We are planning to kick off the questionnaire next Wednesday.

Best,
Sara
Sara Paulson
Senior InfoSec Manager, NorthBridge Financial

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify evidence scope for FedRAMP/ISO review

Sara — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Mina (compliance ops) and Lauren (cert roadmaps) to give concrete artifacts and owners. Quick summary up front:

- Log retention: We maintain 12 months of service-level logs (CloudTrail + VPC flow logs + system access logs) in a secure bucket; for audits we provide immutable snapshots for the requested window. We can also provide targeted extracts for the audit sampling window.
- Evidence matrix: We have an ISO evidence matrix mapped to control IDs (internal matrix + exported CSV). Mina will attach the owner mapping and preferred artifact locations.
- Third-party attestations: Our baseline approach is to accept vendor SOC2/SOC3/SIG attestations as evidence for upstream SaaS components where we do not control the stack. For components in our control plane (managed DBs where we hold credentials or containers we build), we include evidence directly. Where a vendor attestation can be used, we annotate that in the CAIQ/SIG answers so auditors can see the chain of trust.

Action items for our side: Mina to share the evidence matrix and an example logs export procedure; Lauren to confirm FedRAMP snapshot SLA and retention policy doc. Priyom, please pull the latest SIG draft (I think v1) and mark fields that explicitly reference 3P attestations.

Sara — is there a single contact at NorthBridge who will own the SIG intake? If so we can pre-fill some answers.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify evidence scope for FedRAMP/ISO review — matrix & sample artifacts attached

Hi Sara — attaching the artifacts Rishi mentioned. Quick notes inline: 

Attachments (attached to this message):
- SIG-answers-draft-v1.xlsx (draft answers with annotations where we rely on vendor attestations)
- ISO-evidence-matrix-owners.csv (control -> artifact -> owner -> storage location)
- fedramp-log-retention-policy.pdf (policy + how to request immutable snapshots)

Highlights:
- Logs: Our default retention for system/controller logs is 12 months. For FedRAMP customers we can provide snapshots within the audit window within 5 business days. Requests must come with an auditor e-mail and a signed confidentiality agreement (we have a standard stub).
- Evidence matrix: The CSV includes a column "accepts_vendor_attestation" — where true, auditors may accept vendor SOC/SIG. Where false, we provide tenant-level artifacts. Example: managed DB backup integrity checks are tenant-visible, so we ship the artifact; container image provenance may accept a registry's sig if the image is published by a verified vendor and covered by their SOC report.
- Ownership: Each artifact row includes an owner (team + individual). Primary owners for upcoming submissions: Mina Haddad (controls mapping, artifacts), Priyom Das (SIG/CAIQ answers), Lauren Bishop (FedRAMP project manager / audit scheduling).

Please note: some artifacts are redacted for customer privacy in shared examples; for an audit we will provide non-redacted versions under an NDA.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm NorthBridge's intake contact (name, email).
2) Tell us the preferred audit sampling window (e.g., Q1 2026 calendar week 10–12 or specific dates) so we can stage log snapshots.
3) Indicate any specific upstream vendors you want us to include; we'll flag where vendor attestations cover controls.

I'll also add a short how-to doc for requesting a snapshot to the Drive link below.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify evidence scope for FedRAMP/ISO review — timeline and escalation path

Sara — thanks for the prompt. A few practical notes for scheduling and escalation: 

- Timeline: If you plan to start the SIG/CAIQ on Nov 17 we can target providing pre-filled answers and attachments within 3 business days for the prioritized controls (we'll triage high-risk controls first). Full delivery of tenant-specific artifacts and logs will be 5 business days after we receive the signed snapshot NDA and the auditor contact.
- Escalation: If auditors need immediate access to an artifact during an active audit, please route requests to compliance@redwoodinference.com and CC me. We have an audit on-call rotation and a documented SLT escalation path for time-sensitive evidence.
- Sampling: For FedRAMP, we recommend a rolling 30-day sample window across representative weeks rather than one continuous block; that reduces snapshot size while preserving auditor coverage. We'll map the weeks to the log indexes in the attached policy.

Priyom — please confirm the SIG spreadsheet version and mark any fields that require vendor confirmation.

Sara — once you confirm the NorthBridge intake contact and preferred sampling weeks, we'll get the snapshot request queued and lock the artifacts owners into JIRA-SEC-1124.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Certification Program Lead
Redwood Inference
